from datetime import datetime
from google.cloud import monitoring_v3
from observability_client import ObservabilityClient
from observability_models import MetricQueryRequest, MetricStatsResponse

def aggregate_metric_stats(request: MetricQueryRequest) -> MetricStatsResponse:
    client = ObservabilityClient().get_monitoring_client()
    project_name = f"projects/{request.project_id}"

    interval = monitoring_v3.TimeInterval(
        end_time={'seconds': int(request.end_time.timestamp())},
        start_time={'seconds': int(request.start_time.timestamp())}
    )

    query_filter = request.filter if request.filter else f'metric.type = "{request.metric_type}"'

    # Aggregation for statistics
    aggregation = monitoring_v3.Aggregation(
        alignment_period={'seconds': int((request.end_time - request.start_time).total_seconds())},
        per_series_aligner=monitoring_v3.Aggregation.Aligner.ALIGN_MEAN,
        cross_series_reducer=monitoring_v3.Aggregation.Reducer.REDUCE_MEAN,
        group_by_fields=['metric.type']
    )

    # Fetch time series for average
    avg_results = client.list_time_series(
        name=project_name,
        filter=query_filter,
        interval=interval,
        view=monitoring_v3.ListTimeSeriesRequest.TimeSeriesView.FULL,
        aggregation=aggregation
    )

    average_value = None
    if avg_results:
        for ts in avg_results:
            for point in ts.points:
                value = point.int64_value or point.double_value or point.string_value or (point.bool_value if isinstance(point.bool_value, bool) else None)
                if value is not None:
                    average_value = float(value)
                    break
            if average_value is not None:
                break

    # For min, max, sum, count, we need separate queries with different reducers
    min_value, max_value, sum_value, count_value = None, None, None, None

    # Min aggregation
    min_aggregation = monitoring_v3.Aggregation(
        alignment_period={'seconds': int((request.end_time - request.start_time).total_seconds())},
        per_series_aligner=monitoring_v3.Aggregation.Aligner.ALIGN_MIN,
        cross_series_reducer=monitoring_v3.Aggregation.Reducer.REDUCE_MIN,
        group_by_fields=['metric.type']
    )
    min_results = client.list_time_series(
        name=project_name,
        filter=query_filter,
        interval=interval,
        view=monitoring_v3.ListTimeSeriesRequest.TimeSeriesView.FULL,
        aggregation=min_aggregation
    )
    if min_results:
        for ts in min_results:
            for point in ts.points:
                value = point.int64_value or point.double_value or point.string_value or (point.bool_value if isinstance(point.bool_value, bool) else None)
                if value is not None:
                    min_value = float(value)
                    break
            if min_value is not None:
                break

    # Max aggregation
    max_aggregation = monitoring_v3.Aggregation(
        alignment_period={'seconds': int((request.end_time - request.start_time).total_seconds())},
        per_series_aligner=monitoring_v3.Aggregation.Aligner.ALIGN_MAX,
        cross_series_reducer=monitoring_v3.Aggregation.Reducer.REDUCE_MAX,
        group_by_fields=['metric.type']
    )
    max_results = client.list_time_series(
        name=project_name,
        filter=query_filter,
        interval=interval,
        view=monitoring_v3.ListTimeSeriesRequest.TimeSeriesView.FULL,
        aggregation=max_aggregation
    )
    if max_results:
        for ts in max_results:
            for point in ts.points:
                value = point.int64_value or point.double_value or point.string_value or (point.bool_value if isinstance(point.bool_value, bool) else None)
                if value is not None:
                    max_value = float(value)
                    break
            if max_value is not None:
                break

    # Sum aggregation
    sum_aggregation = monitoring_v3.Aggregation(
        alignment_period={'seconds': int((request.end_time - request.start_time).total_seconds())},
        per_series_aligner=monitoring_v3.Aggregation.Aligner.ALIGN_SUM,
        cross_series_reducer=monitoring_v3.Aggregation.Reducer.REDUCE_SUM,
        group_by_fields=['metric.type']
    )
    sum_results = client.list_time_series(
        name=project_name,
        filter=query_filter,
        interval=interval,
        view=monitoring_v3.ListTimeSeriesRequest.TimeSeriesView.FULL,
        aggregation=sum_aggregation
    )
    if sum_results:
        for ts in sum_results:
            for point in ts.points:
                value = point.int64_value or point.double_value or point.string_value or (point.bool_value if isinstance(point.bool_value, bool) else None)
                if value is not None:
                    sum_value = float(value)
                    break
            if sum_value is not None:
                break

    # Count aggregation
    count_aggregation = monitoring_v3.Aggregation(
        alignment_period={'seconds': int((request.end_time - request.start_time).total_seconds())},
        per_series_aligner=monitoring_v3.Aggregation.Aligner.ALIGN_COUNT,
        cross_series_reducer=monitoring_v3.Aggregation.Reducer.REDUCE_SUM,
        group_by_fields=['metric.type']
    )
    count_results = client.list_time_series(
        name=project_name,
        filter=query_filter,
        interval=interval,
        view=monitoring_v3.ListTimeSeriesRequest.TimeSeriesView.FULL,
        aggregation=count_aggregation
    )
    if count_results:
        for ts in count_results:
            for point in ts.points:
                value = point.int64_value or point.double_value or point.string_value or (point.bool_value if isinstance(point.bool_value, bool) else None)
                if value is not None:
                    count_value = int(value)
                    break
            if count_value is not None:
                break

    return MetricStatsResponse(
        metric_type=request.metric_type,
        start_time=request.start_time,
        end_time=request.end_time,
        average=average_value,
        min=min_value,
        max=max_value,
        sum=sum_value,
        count=count_value

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Optional
from google.cloud import aiplatform
from observability_models import TimeSeries

@dataclass
class MetricSummaryRequest:
    project_id: str
    location: str # e.g., us-central1
    metric_data: List[TimeSeries]

@dataclass
class MetricSummaryResponse:
    summary: str
    anomaly_detected: bool

def summarize_metric_trends(request: MetricSummaryRequest) -> MetricSummaryResponse:
    aiplatform.init(project=request.project_id, location=request.location)

    # For demonstration, we'll simulate a prompt based on the time series data
    # In a real scenario, you'd feed more sophisticated data points and context
    metric_info = []
    for ts in request.metric_data:
        metric_name = ts.metric_labels.get('metric_name', 'unknown_metric')
        resource_id = ts.resource_labels.get('resource_id', 'unknown_resource')
        values = [str(p.value) for p in ts.points]
        metric_info.append(f"Metric '{metric_name}' on resource '{resource_id}' has values: {', '.join(values[:10])}...")

    prompt_text = (f"Summarize the following metric trends and identify any anomalies:\n\n"
                   f"{'; '.join(metric_info)}\n\nSummary:")

    # Using a pre-trained text generation model from Vertex AI
    # Replace 'text-bison@001' with an appropriate model for summarization
    # For actual anomaly detection, a more complex model or rule-based system would be needed
    model = aiplatform.PredictionServiceClient(client_options={"api_endpoint": f"{request.location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"})
    endpoint = f"projects/{request.project_id}/locations/{request.location}/publishers/google/models/text-bison@001"

    response = model.predict(
        endpoint=endpoint,
        instances=[{"prompt": prompt_text}],
        parameters={"temperature": 0.2, "maxOutputTokens": 200, "topK": 40, "topP": 0.95}
    )

    summary_text = response.predictions[0]["content"]

    # Simple heuristic for anomaly detection for demonstration purposes
    anomaly_detected = "anomaly" in summary_text.lower() or "unusual" in summary_text.lower()

    return MetricSummaryResponse(summary=summary_text, anomaly_detected=anomaly_detected)

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List
from google.cloud import aiplatform

@dataclass
class AnnotationSafetyRequest:
    project_id: str
    location: str  # e.g., us-central1
    annotations: List[str]

@dataclass
class AnnotationSafetyResponse:
    checked_annotations: List[str]
    unsafe_annotations: List[str]
    safety_scores: List[dict]

def check_annotation_safety(request: AnnotationSafetyRequest) -> AnnotationSafetyResponse:
    aiplatform.init(project=request.project_id, location=request.location)

    unsafe_annotations = []
    safety_scores_list = []

    # Using a pre-trained text generation model from Vertex AI for content safety analysis
    # For robust content moderation, Google Cloud's specialized Content Warehouse or an abuse detection API would be more appropriate.
    # Here, we simulate a safety check using a general model with specific prompting.
    model = aiplatform.PredictionServiceClient(client_options={"api_endpoint": f"{request.location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"})
    endpoint = f"projects/{request.project_id}/locations/{request.location}/publishers/google/models/text-bison@001"

    for annotation_text in request.annotations:
        prompt_text = (
            f"Analyze the following text for safety. Respond with 'SAFE' if the text contains no harmful, "
            f"abusive, or inappropriate content. Respond with 'UNSAFE' otherwise. "
            f"Provide a brief reason if it's UNSAFE.\n\nText: '{annotation_text}'\nAnalysis:"
        )

        response = model.predict(
            endpoint=endpoint,
            instances=[{"prompt": prompt_text}],
            parameters={"temperature": 0.1, "maxOutputTokens": 100, "topK": 40, "topP": 0.95}
        )

        analysis_result = response.predictions[0]["content"].strip()
        
        is_unsafe = "UNSAFE" in analysis_result.upper()
        if is_unsafe:
            unsafe_annotations.append(annotation_text)
        
        safety_scores_list.append({
            "annotation": annotation_text,
            "is_unsafe": is_unsafe,
            "analysis": analysis_result
        })

    return AnnotationSafetyResponse(
        checked_annotations=request.annotations,
        unsafe_annotations=unsafe_annotations,
        safety_scores=safety_scores_list
    )

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, Any
from google.cloud import storage

@dataclass
class MetricExportArchiveRequest:
    project_id: str
    bucket_name: str
    destination_blob_name: str # e.g., metrics_snapshots/2023/04/snapshot_2023-04-23.json
    data_to_archive: str # The content of the snapshot, e.g., JSON string
    content_type: str = "application/json" # e.g., application/json, text/csv

@dataclass
class MetricExportArchiveResponse:
    bucket_name: str
    blob_name: str
    uri: str
    size_bytes: int
    time_created: datetime

def archive_metric_snapshot(request: MetricExportArchiveRequest) -> MetricExportArchiveResponse:
    storage_client = storage.Client(project=request.project_id)
    bucket = storage_client.bucket(request.bucket_name)
    blob = bucket.blob(request.destination_blob_name)

    blob.upload_from_string(request.data_to_archive, content_type=request.content_type)

    # Refresh the blob's metadata to get updated information like size and creation time
    blob.reload()

    return MetricExportArchiveResponse(
        bucket_name=request.bucket_name,
        blob_name=request.destination_blob_name,
        uri=f"gs://{request.bucket_name}/{request.destination_blob_name}",
        size_bytes=blob.size,
        time_created=blob.time_created
    )
